options.text: On the steel plate the water mainly evaporates into the air.
On the steel plate the water seeps into the metal, just as it seeps into soil.
On the soil the water can both seep in and evaporate.
Neither case involves evaporation, because no white mist was visible.

stem:
Mohan spills the same small amount of water on a polished steel plate and on dry garden soil. After some time both wet patches look smaller.

Which claims correctly explain the disappearing water? One or more options may be correct.

teacher.key_rationale: On impermeable steel, water mainly evaporates. On soil, water can seep in and also evaporate. Steel does not take in water like soil, and mist is not required to show evaporation.
